key_insight: CROSS is a culture-aware, cross-modal framework that decodes symbolic and contextual cues in memes to detect harmful intent while producing interpretable explanations—closing gaps in cultural blindness, boundary ambiguity, and opaque reasoning.
problem_solved: Identifies implicit, culturally-encoded social abuse in memes where harm depends on symbols, jokes, or image–text incongruence, and disambiguates satire from genuine abuse with explainable outputs.
method: Augments multimodal representations with symbol- and culture-aware knowledge to recognize contextual references and symbolic meaning in images and text.
Detects cross-modal incongruence using contrastive alignment and a boundary-aware classifier that separates satirical/benign uses from abusive intent.
Generates interpretable explanations (symbol-level attributions, attention/heatmap overlays, and short natural-language rationales) to justify decisions.
impact: Makes meme moderation and multimodal safety systems more culturally sensitive, accurate, and auditable—reducing false positives/negatives and enabling trustable deployment of LVLMs in real-world content moderation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input meme → symbol/cultural encoder → cross-modal alignment → classifier → interpretable rationale
Before/after meme examples with detected symbols highlighted and short model rationales (satire vs abuse)
Attention/heatmap overlays showing which image regions and text tokens drove the decision
Bar/confusion-chart comparing error rates on satire vs abuse separation between baseline and CROSS
paper_title: They Said Memes Were Harmless-We Found the Ones That Hurt: Decoding Jokes, Symbols, and Cultural References
paper_authors: Sahil Tripathi, Gautam Siddharth Kashyap, Mehwish Nasim, Jian Yang, Jiechao Gao
